name: Galbijjim: Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs
why: Galbijjim is the classic Korean festive braise — deeply savoury beef short ribs simmered with a pear-kiwi enzyme sauce, jujubes, chestnuts and ginkgo nuts. A perfect autumn showpiece that leans into seasonal ingredients, and a great technique lesson in how fruit breaks down meat while kelp stock deepens the umami.
author: Henry
ingredients: 3-1/2 to 4 lbs (1.5-1.8 kg) beef short ribs (Korean style preferred)
1/2 Korean pear, peeled, seeded and diced
1 large piece (10-15 g) dried sea kelp (dashima)
2 carrots, peeled and cut into big chunks
3/4 lb (340 g) Korean radish (or white daikon), peeled and cut into chunks
6 shiitake mushrooms, stems trimmed (fresh or rehydrated dried)
Chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds, for garnish

steps: Parboil the short ribs: place them in a large pot of water and boil for about 10 minutes over medium-high heat to remove impurities and excess fat. Drain and rinse under running water, scrubbing off any bone fragments.
Cut a few shallow 1/2-inch slits into the ribs so they absorb the braising sauce better.

Make the sea kelp stock: simmer the dried kelp (dashima) in 4 cups of water over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, then remove and discard the kelp. Measure out 2-1/2 cups of stock — the rest is for the sauce.
Blend the braising sauce: in a blender or food processor, combine the onion, pear, kiwi, garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice wine and 1/2 cup of the kelp stock until completely smooth.
Trim the edges of the carrot and radish chunks so they hold their shape, and cross-score the tops of the shiitake for a decorative finish.
Place the parboiled ribs in a Dutch oven or heavy pot, pour over the blended sauce, and add the remaining 2 cups of kelp stock, ginger paste, sesame oil and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for about 1-1/2 hours, skimming off fat from the surface now and then.
Add the carrots and radishes and continue simmering for 20-30 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender. If using rehydrated dried shiitake, add them now.
Stir in the fresh shiitake, jujubes, chestnuts and ginkgo nuts and cook for another 10-15 minutes until everything is glossy and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Remove from the heat and let the braise rest for 10 minutes so the flavours meld — the meat should be fork-tender and falling off the bone.
Garnish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve warm with steamed rice and kimchi on the side.

pro_tips: The pear and kiwi are not there for sweetness — their natural enzymes break down collagen while it simmers, which is why the ribs come out silk-tender. Don't substitute apple; the enzymes do the real work.

If you can't find Korean-style thin-cut short ribs, boneless beef ribs work fine — just trim more fat after parboiling. Ginkgo nuts can be bought pre-roasted; the jujubes and chestnuts are the seasonal heart of this dish and worth the trip to an Asian supermarket.
